accepted.evidence: Andersen prints tathā 'so, thus' beside RV/Pali tathā and regionally varying tatha/tathā forms. Turner 5646 táthā directly gives Pali tathā and Ashokan tatha with variable final length; preserve this attested adverb as its own source head.
The Nittur line on the preceding scan page says 'see tatha' and is the source's unglossed counterpart to the 'so, thus' head. Turner 5646 explicitly notes Ashokan variable final vowel length.

Andersen's separate ve line says '(Skt vaḥ) see tu-' and its pronoun paradigm labels ve accusative/dative plural. Turner 11183 vaḥ is the enclitic second-person plural pronoun and explicitly lists Ashokan ve dative.

Andersen's separately bounded printed sata entry is glossed 'hundred', compares RV śatá and Pali sata, and cites Rupnath. Turner 12278 śatá '100' lists Pali sata and Ashokan śata/ṣata regional series; direct scan inspection resolves the earlier cached-OCR boundary concern.
